liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bertha** (3 reviews): This version is used on the Skull & Roses LP; This is the version released on the double album in November 1971 [14][21][22]
- **Hard To Handle** (3 reviews): Lesh and Garcia build tension before launching into the Theme at full bore; Best version ever heard; Garcia and Lesh lead two passes through the Theme [13][14][19]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Opening version is on par with any other [14]
- **Searchin'** (1 review): Must-hear version for rock, blues, and country fans [11]
- **Good Vibrations** (1 review): Moog covered the theremin part; Beach Boys shone while Dead took a break [12]
- **Help Me Rhonda** (1 review): Listener loves this version of Help Me Rhonda [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-04-27.sbd.gadsden-oleynick.5165.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 41 songs; 261 min [1]
- **gd71-04-27.sbd.murphy.2221.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 34 songs; 225 min; rated 4.19/5 by 21 [2]
- **gd1971-04-27.sbd.bode-hoffman-merryprankster-stundel.2998.shnf**: soundboard; 27 songs; 184 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [8]
- **gd1971-04-27.152206.BerthaRoughMixes.studio.bershaw.flac16**: source not stated; 2 songs; 7 min [10]. Said about its sound: Merl Saunders' organ is significantly more pronounced than in the released album version; Tuning prior to the song beginning was edited out from the final album mix [10]

## Around the show

- Beach Boys joined the Dead, blending West Coast and previous revolution styles [11]
- Beach Boys brought a Moog synthesizer, used as slide whistle and siren [12]
- Garcia announced the Beach Boys; the crowd booed, thinking it a letdown [15]
- Word 'Dylan' appeared on the backdrop as the Beach Boys set ended [15]
- New manager Jack Riely pushed the Beach Boys onstage, telling them to get hip [16]
- Riely saved the Beach Boys from being stuck playing oldies in white suits [16]
- NRPS opened with Jerry Garcia on pedal steel [17]
- Beach Boys joined the Dead for several tunes in the second set [17]
- This version has the Theme better than the 4/29 show [13]
- This Hard to Handle is better than the August 1971 Hollywood show version [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-04-27.sbd.gadsden-oleynick.5165.shnf**: source: NRPS: MR>C>CDRx?>SHN, Truckin' through Loser: MR>CDR>SHN , Hard to Handle through Lovelight: MR>R>CDR>SHN. GD SBD>MR : Shure line mixers > Sony reel to reel… [1]. Also: Tapes originated from a cabinetmaker who had Fillmore East composites from 1971; Three 90-minute composites of the 1971 shows circulated for about a year [1]
- **gd71-04-27.sbd.murphy.2221.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bob Murphy; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Source is MSR 7-inch tape, transferred via Revox A 77 and Alesis Masterlink; Tapes provided via Bob Murphy; details reference Bill Gadsden's notes [2]
- **gd1971-04-27.sbd.bode-hoffman-merryprankster-stundel.2998.shnf**: transferred by Abe Stundel; source: SBD>MR>R>D>CD [8]. Also: Disks from Keith Bode, sourced from Justin Hoffman, originally from Merry Prankster's Tree; Transferred by Abe Stundel using EAC to SHN format [8]
- **gd1971-04-27.152206.BerthaRoughMixes.studio.bershaw.flac16**: transferred by Alan Bershaw; source: Alan Bershaw's low generation cassette (Maxell UDXL2 w/Dolby B) [10]
- Parts of this show were officially released on Ladies and Gentleman, The Grateful Dead [26]
- Bertha from that night kicks off the Grateful Dead (Skull and Roses) Expanded Edition [28]

## Art and photos

- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1971-04-27 Fillmore East, New York, NY](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/07/grateful-dead-1971-04-27-fillmore-east.html) [29]
